simple.meaning: נָכֹחַ (nâkôach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “straightforward , i.e. (figuratively), equitable , correct , or (abstractly), integrity.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across 2 Samuel, Proverbs, Isaiah, beginning at 2 Samuel 15:3. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָכֹחַ (H5228).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָכֹחַ (nâkôach) / H5228 is traced through 2 Samuel 15:3, Proverbs 8:9, Proverbs 24:26, Isaiah 57:2 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: straightforward , i.e. (figuratively), equitable , correct , or (abstractly), integrity
definitions.full: H5228. nakoach [ נָכֹחַ ] adjective and substantive straight, right, straightness , feminine נְכֹחָה , plural וֺת נְכֹחִים, -: — Isa 57:2 נְכֹחוֺ הֹלֵךְ he that walks in (compare 33:15 ; 50:10 ) his straightness (Ges 'der seinen geraden Weg geht'), figurative for straightforwardly (compare Prov 4:25 ); נְכֹחָה what is straight in front , figurative straightforwardness, honesty , Amos 3:10 נ עֲשׂוֺת יָָֽדְעוּ ׳לֹא , Isa 59:14 ׳ונ לָבוֺא תוּכַל לֹא (|| אֱמֶת ); 2Sam 15:3 וּנְכֹחִים טובים דבריך thy pleadings are good and right (i.e. TRUE ), Prov 8:9 (of words of Wisdom) לַמֵּבִין נְכֹחִים כֻּלָּם i.e. they lead straight to the right goal (|| ישׁרים ; compare 8:8 b וְעִקֵּשׁ נִפָתָּל בָּהֶם אֵין ), 24:26 נְכֹחִים דְּבָרִים מֵשִׁיב i.e. either correct (leading to the right point), or honest answers; Isa 30:10 נְכֹחוֺת לָנוּ לֹאתֶֿחֱזוּ TRUE things (opposed to מַהֲתַלּוֺת חֲלָקוֺת, illusions ), 26:10 יְעַוֵּל נְכֹחוֺת בְּאֶרֶץ in a land of rectitude (Che) he will do wickedly.

occurrences.englishText: Absalom said to him, “Behold, your matters are good and right; but there is no man deputized by the king to hear you.”
They are all plain to him who understands,
